title: EU Egress Governance Broker and Tenant Allow/Deny Adapter
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers operating under EU data laws require deterministic egress decisions (route to EU-only hosting, block or allow per-tenant rules) and predictable model fallbacks when preferred EU variants are unavailable. Current routing is region-preference based and lacks a composable layer that combines: tenant-level allow/deny lists, contractual residency gates, and a pluggable fallback model shim that preserves data residency guarantees where required.

Goal: Implement an Egress Governance Broker (EGB) service and a Tenant Allow/Deny Adapter (TADA) to enforce per-tenant EU-only routing constraints and to orchestrate safe fallback model variants without violating residency constraints. The EGB should be policy-driven, auditable, and integrated into the request path before model selection and scheduling.

Scope: MVP covers the following capabilities: tenant-level permit/deny evaluation, contract-tag-aware routing (e.g., "eu-only", "eu-preferred"), model-variant fallback policy that respects residency and tier constraints, audit logging for policy decisions, and admin APIs for allow/deny rule management. Does not cover UI for rule management (Console work will be tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: EGB evaluates tenant metadata and returns a routing decision (EU, GLOBAL, BLOCK) within 5ms tail for 99% requests under standard load
Tenant rules can be created/updated via admin API and are versioned for audit
If EU-only is required and EU capacity is full, request is rejected or routed to a pre-approved on-prem/private endpoint per tenant settings
Fallback model variants are selected such that data never exits EU when tenant policy forbids it
All policy decisions emit structured audit events to the observability pipeline (request id, tenant id, decision, reason)
Integration tests cover permit -> route mappings, deny -> block behavior, and fallback path selection
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight EGB microservice in the control plane with an in-memory policy cache and eventual consistent backing store (Postgres) for rules
Policy schema: tenant_id, rule_type (allow|deny), tag_scope (egress_region), expiration, operator, created_by, audit_version
Policy evaluation will short-circuit: explicit deny -> block, explicit allow -> honor, else consult contract_tag (eu-only/eu-preferred) -> route decision

EGB will expose a sync gRPC endpoint used by the router/runtime. Router will call EGB during request admission to get a RouteDecision (string) and allowed_model_variants (list-of-ids-as-csv in header)

Fallback model shim: map 'preferred_model_id' -> ['eu_variant_v2', 'eu_variant_v1', 'private_onprem_model'] with explicit residency labels. Router must not select any model without matching residency label if tenant requires eu-only
Add circuit-breaker metrics for when EU pool is full to trigger admin notifications and optional automatic enqueue for dedicated capacity purchases
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy EGB to control plane in us-west-2 + eu-west-1 read replicas. Feature flag (egress_gov) off by default. Route 1% of traffic for test tenant set.
Phase 2 (expanded): Enable for internal Redwood tenants and 10 pilot customers with varying policies. Collect latency and false-block metrics.
Phase 3 (opt-in GA): Expose admin API to customers via Support/SEs, enable console UI work collaboration with PM/Design.

Rollback: Feature flag kill-switch and policy version rollback endpoint. If policy-error rate > 0.5% for 10m, auto-disable and fail open to previous routing behavior (unless tenant-level deny exists).
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation engine (allow/deny/contract tag precedence)
Integration test: router <-> EGB interaction with mocked EU fullness signals
End-to-end test: create tenant rule EU-only, exhaust EU capacity in test env, verify either block or onprem fallback per tenant setting
Load test: policy evaluation under 5000 rps synthetic workload; measure p95 latency
Security test: verify admin APIs require SSO with RBAC and KMS-signed audit events
